definition: Brief visit for a single minor complaint, with a focused history or examination of one part of the body.
Standard office visit: history of the presenting complaint, examination of one or more systems, and advice or a prescription. The default visit code when no more specific code applies.
Full history and examination of all body systems for a new or complex problem, including review of past history, medications and family history.
Scheduled preventive visit for an adult, with age-appropriate screening, immunization review and counselling.
Scheduled well-child visit with growth, development and immunization review.
Assessment requested in writing by another physician, with a written report back to the referring physician.
Further assessment of the same problem for the same referring physician within 12 months of a consultation.

Visit focused on diabetes care: review of glucose readings or log, A1c and other results, adjustment of diabetes medication, and counselling on diet, exercise or self-management. Billed with a diabetes diagnostic code.
Visit focused on heart failure care: volume status, daily weights, adjustment of heart failure medication and patient education. Billed with a heart failure diagnostic code.

Dedicated counselling to help a patient quit tobacco: readiness, quit date, pharmacotherapy options and relapse prevention. Billed in addition to the visit when at least 10 minutes are spent on counselling.
Follow-up counselling session for a patient in an active quit attempt.
Counselling of a patient on a medical problem, lifestyle or treatment, per unit of at least 20 minutes, when counselling is most of the visit.
Structured psychotherapy or mental health counselling with one patient, per unit of at least 30 minutes.
Office visit within 14 days of a hospital discharge, including reconciliation of discharge medications against the discharge summary.
Structured review of all of a patient's medications for interactions, duplication, adherence and deprescribing.
Recording of a 12-lead ECG in the office.
Physician interpretation and written report of a 12-lead ECG.
Pulmonary function testing with spirometry, before and after bronchodilator, with interpretation.
Administration of a vaccine by injection, with or without a visit on the same day.
Administration of a therapeutic injection other than a vaccine.
Assessment by secure video when the patient is not in the office.
Assessment by telephone when the patient is not in the office.
Completion of a workplace injury or insurance form, billed to the workplace insurer rather than the provincial plan.
Completion of a form or letter not covered by the plan, billed to the patient or a third party.
Routine antenatal visit during pregnancy.
Visit with a clinic nurse for a blood pressure check, injection, dressing or education, under physician supervision.
